title: DEPTH 14 (dim 896, 14 heads) + HEAD_DIM 64
description: DEPTH 10->14 (n_embd 640->896), HEAD_DIM 128->64 (14 heads), DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64->32 (grad_accum 2->4, same 2^18 total batch); no other changes.
reflection: Strong NEGATIVE and a useful bracket: val_bpb 1.033838 vs the 0.988076 depth-10 baseline, +0.0458 (~65 sigma against the 7e-4 noise floor). 476 steps, 124.8M tokens, 200.9M params, MFU 43.25% (the highest in the cell so far), peak VRAM only 34.4GB at device batch 32. Throughput is emphatically not the problem -- MFU rose monotonically with size across the cell (37.7% at d8, 41.9% at d10, 43.3% at d14). The problem is data starvation: tokens-per-parameter falls 9.3 (d8) -> 3.4 (d10) -> 0.62 (d14), and val_bpb tracks that, not FLOP efficiency. So the size axis is now bracketed hard: depth 8 (0.9935 with HD64) < depth 10 (0.9881) << depth 14 (1.0338). The compute-optimal point at a 5-minute budget sits at or just above depth 10; depth 14 is far past it, and nothing above 12 is worth another slot. Also worth recording: HEAD_DIM 64 was folded in here, so this is not a clean single-variable read on depth alone -- but the effect is 12x larger than the measured HD64 benefit and in the opposite direction, so the sign is not in doubt.
